Candidate.description:
A ranked record.

Exact-ID hits rank first in request order, then records matched directly by the
lexical or semantic channel, then records reached only through the graph. Within
a tier, ties on ``relevance_score`` are broken by ascending CVE ID.

missing_fields.description: Record fields no source supplied; unknown, not evidence of low risk.
missing_fields.title: Missing Fields

relevance_score.description: Reciprocal-rank-fusion score over the exact-ID, lexical, semantic and graph hits. Measures relevance to the query only — not severity, exploitability or confidence. Structured hits record why the candidate satisfied the filters and add no score.
relevance_score.title: Relevance Score

weakness_associations.description: Full catalogue-derived paths on single-CVE lookup only; omitted from search, topic and investigation candidates, including excluded candidates. Separate from retrieval evidence and FiGHT protocol context.

Candidate.title: Candidate

matched_terms.description: Terms the server can vouch for: the caller's query terms (lexical) or filter values (structured), relation values both records carry (graph), or the requested CVE ID; none for the semantic channel.
matched_terms.title: Matched Terms

raw_score.description: The channel's own score; scales differ by channel.
raw_score.title: Raw Score

detail.description: The server's sentence for why the channel failed; null when it answered.

CveRecord.description:
An implementation-level vulnerability record.

``protocol_design_claim`` and ``formal_seed_eligible`` are fixed: a CVE never
establishes a protocol-design vulnerability and never seeds formal analysis.

kev.description: CISA KEV entry, when a consulted source lists one.

CveRecord.title: CveRecord

EvidenceAnchor.description: A pointer to one source record, precise enough to re-fetch and re-hash it.

authoritative_record_id.description: Identifier of the record in its source of record, e.g. a CVE ID.
authoritative_record_id.title: Authoritative Record Id

content_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the source record this anchor points at.
content_sha256.title: Content Sha256

evidence_id.description: 'ev:' and the first 24 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of every other anchor field; it changes when any provenance field changes. The server re-derives it and rejects a mismatch. An integrity check, not proof of origin: a holder can recompute it.
evidence_id.title: Evidence Id

excerpt.description: Bounded excerpt, present only when the source's terms permit redistribution.
excerpt.title: Excerpt

inference_method.description: How an inferred anchor was derived; required iff inferred.
inference_method.title: Inference Method

locator.description: Field path or JSON pointer inside the source.
locator.title: Locator

source_version.description: Release, commit, ETag or snapshot identifier, when the source exposes one.
source_version.title: Source Version

EvidenceAnchor.title: EvidenceAnchor

GraphPath.description: One asserted relation a graph hit shares with the seed record it was reached from.
GraphPath.title: GraphPath

known_ransomware_campaign_use.description: CISA's own Known/Unknown assessment; null when the consulted source does not carry it.
known_ransomware_campaign_use.title: Known Ransomware Campaign Use

KnowledgeScope.description: What kind of knowledge a record, evidence anchor or claim represents.
KnowledgeScope.title: KnowledgeScope

source.description: Who authored this text, e.g. a CNA.
source.title: Source

MatchedField.description:

ObservationStatus.description: FiGHT's own maturity label, normalized; ``source_status`` keeps the original text.
ObservationStatus.title: ObservationStatus

matched_terms.description: Card terms (alias, entity or ecosystem term), or a qualifying network-function abbreviation, found in the record.
matched_terms.title: Matched Terms

RelevanceTier.description: How a candidate relates to a topic. Relevance only: never severity or affectedness.
RelevanceTier.title: RelevanceTier

SourceOutcome.description:
What one knowledge source answered. Every word of it is the server's: a failed
FiGHT source and the affectedness source carry one of the server's sentences in
``detail``, and a CVE search lists its channels' failures in ``channel_failures``.

channel_failures.description: Each distinct failure of a cve_search's channels, once; a channel that failed in different ways appears once per way. Empty for other sources.
channel_failures.title: Channel Failures

coverage.description: The coverage type of the snapshot consulted: full for the whole catalogued upstream file, excerpt for a reviewed cut of one. It never says the response lists every match; truncation warnings say what a limit left out.

detail.description: The server's sentence for why the source gave no answer: an AffectednessDetail for affectedness, a BackendFailureDetail for mitre_fight, and null for cve_search, whose failures are its channel_failures.
detail.title: Detail

source_version.description: Snapshot identity of the source consulted, when it has one.
source_version.title: Source Version

SourceOutcome.title: SourceOutcome

SourceType.description: Kind of source an evidence anchor points into. Values are added with their adapters.
SourceType.title: SourceType

TechniqueField.description: A field of a FiGHT technique a search can match, so no source names anything else.
TechniqueField.title: TechniqueField

matched_terms.description: Terms the server sent to FiGHT that the technique holds: a resolved topic's name, aliases and entities, or with no topic the question's own words.
matched_terms.title: Matched Terms

source_status.description: The status text exactly as published.
source_status.title: Source Status

candidate.description: The candidate from its best-ranked search.

retrieval_channels.description: Every channel that retrieved the record, in any template.
retrieval_channels.title: Retrieval Channels

topic_rank.description: Order by relevance tier, then search rank, then CVE ID.
topic_rank.title: Topic Rank

TopicContextWarning.description:
What a response leaves out or could not do. ``protocol_context_truncated`` counts
the techniques the snapshot matched that the protocol section does not list because
of the response's bounds; ``candidates_truncated`` the relevant CVEs topic context
held that the candidate section does not list only because of its limit, never a
backend's own uncounted matches; ``unrelated_candidates_dropped`` the candidates the
relevance rule removed. ``term_not_indexed`` names a word a direct FiGHT search sent
that no technique holds; a topic's card search never raises it.
``result_limit_reached`` names ``max_results_per_search`` when a card's CVE search
warned it reached that limit, so more matches may exist; it never counts them. A cut changes no
status. ``topic_family_scope`` explains that the matched GTP alias retrieves the
whole family, including GTP-C and GTP-U.
TopicContextWarning.title: TopicContextWarning

context_terms.description: Context terms that licensed a contextual alias.
context_terms.title: Context Terms

matched_alias.description: The card's alias or name that matched.
matched_alias.title: Matched Alias

TopicResolution.description: Every topic the query names, and every excluded term it used instead.
TopicResolution.title: TopicResolution

TrustLevel.description: How far a consumer may rely on an evidence anchor's source.
TrustLevel.title: TrustLevel

VersionRange.description: One affected version or bounded range; at least one bound or ``exact`` is set.
VersionRange.title: VersionRange

VulnerabilityOrigin.description: Where a CVE's defect lives. A CVE never describes a protocol-design flaw here.
VulnerabilityOrigin.title: VulnerabilityOrigin

inherited_from_cwe.description: Linked CWE ancestor used for hierarchy inference, not a direct catalogue link.
inherited_from_cwe.title: Inherited From Cwe

terminal_reason.description: No usable ATT&CK mapping in the loaded catalogue snapshot.
terminal_reason.title: Terminal Reason

note.const: This association is derived from official catalogues. It is not evidence that the CVE was used with that technique. It is not an attack path. No ATT&CK mapping describes only the loaded catalogue snapshot; it does not mean the weakness has no attack technique or no way to be exploited. CWE inheritance is an inference along the CWE hierarchy, not a catalogue link from the original CWE to CAPEC.

note.title: Note
